caption: R6 400 left on paper and the horse still needs shoes. Does a bigger salary just come with a bigger hobby?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R47 500
p/m salary
Living in Hartbeespoort
slides.body:
Female, 34
Single, no kids
Job: Large-animal vet at a country practice
Net salary: R47 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: A cottage on a smallholding, water and borehole
slides.body: I'm 12 minutes from the practice. It's the only reason I can answer calls at 3am.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My parents' farm in the Free State, a drought and a bad season
slides.body: They didn't ask. My brother told me. I'd rather it was a conversation but it's easier as a debit order.

slides.title: Horse
slides.includes: Livery, feed, the farrier every six weeks
slides.body: He's been with me since I was 19. It's R3 900 a month and I've never once regretted it, which is the problem.

slides.title: Student loan
slides.body: Six more years. It doesn't feel like debt, it feels like rent on the past.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Woolies, a butcher, the dog's food (she eats better than I do)
slides.body: R3 200 for one person. I eat out of one pan.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & car insurance, medical aid, electricity, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, savings
slides.body: R4 000 of that is savings. It's the one line where I'm not being honest about how often I skip it.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R47 500. On paper I'm very fine. In practice a vet's income is feast and famine.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction.

The horse is one number now. I can't unsee it.

No bank login needed.
